papers.title_in_file: Defining the quantum workforce landscape: a review of global quantum education initiatives
papers.version_note: arXiv:2202.08940v3, 21 Apr 2022; text matches the record.
papers.what_it_is: A review by QURECA authors of quantum job-vacancy requirements, career pathways and worldwide quantum education and training resources.

assertions.value: The authors state that the study addresses three questions: the competences and education needs of the current quantum ecosystem, the best path to bridge academia and industry, and where to find learning and training resources for a career in quantum technologies.
quotes: we address three main questions in this study
identify and assess the current quantum ecosystem’s competences and education needs
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state their own aims in Section 2.

assertions.value: The authors report that job-vacancy data came from the Quantum Computing Report jobs database, that academic and non-profit vacancies were excluded, and that the search was limited to vacancies in quantum companies.
quotes: the Quantum Computing Report jobs database was accessed for collecting data on commercial job vacancies.
The database search excluded job vacancies from academic and non-
was limited to job vacancies in the quantum companies.
assertions.certainty_reason: Section 2 states how the vacancy data were collected.
assertions.reader_inference: The sample is therefore commercial quantum-company vacancies only; academic hiring is outside it.

assertions.value: The authors state that they evaluated the minimal qualifying criteria of degrees as well as professional experience in the vacancies, and that they did not assess skills demand, which they call beyond the scope of the paper.
quotes: we evaluated the minimal qualifying criteria of
degrees as well as professional experiences.
Although it would be insightful to observe the importance of skills demand for various job vacancies, this assessment is beyond the scope of this paper.
It should be noted that this analysis do not focus on skills needs, but rather on academic degree requirements.
assertions.certainty_reason: Sections 2 and 3 state what the vacancy analysis does and does not cover.

assertions.value: The authors report that they gathered education initiatives from publicly available resources, web searches, journal publications, community events or conferences, and academic and industrial collaboration during the period of 2019-2022.
quotes: We gradually gathered all the education initiatives through publicly available resources, web searches, journal publications, community events or conferences, and academic and industrial collaboration during the period of 2019-2022.
assertions.certainty_reason: Section 2 states how the initiatives were collected.
assertions.reader_inference: No search protocol, inclusion rule or count of screened items is given in the text, so the collection is not reproducible from the paper.

assertions.value: The authors state, as the main limitation, that the study is highly representative in their belief but cannot be argued to be exhaustive, and that the overview is a summary at the time of writing with additional resources to appear later.
quotes: As the main limitation of our study, although we believe it is highly representative, we cannot argue that it is exhaustive.
it should be noted that our overview provides a summary at the time this paper is written, and additional resources will appear in the future.
assertions.certainty_reason: Section 2 states the limitation.
assertions.reader_inference: The same section says the authors reviewed all quantum initiatives currently active, and Section 5.5 calls Fig. 5 a comprehensive list; these wordings sit uneasily with the stated non-exhaustive limit.

assertions.value: The authors state that a detailed overview of education initiatives for current high school and primary school students falls beyond the scope of the paper.
quotes: the detailed overview of education initiatives at this level falls beyond the scope of this paper.
assertions.certainty_reason: Section 7 states what the paper leaves out.

assertions.value: The authors report that they investigated over 750 vacancies and that 62 percent demand a PhD degree.
assertions.anchor: Section 3, p.6; Fig. 1 (pie chart labels in the text layer, panel mapping not recoverable)
quotes: We investigated over 750 vacancies currently available of which 62 percent demand the candidates for a PhD degree.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical count from one vacancy snapshot of one database, with no collection date given in the text.
assertions.reader_inference: The Fig. 1 text layer carries PhD labels of 52%, 61% and 67% for the three panels; which panel is which cannot be recovered from the text layer, and the 62% in the text is the only figure usable in a value. The paper gives no date for the snapshot.

assertions.value: The authors report that graduates with PhD degrees are by far the most in demand among the vacancies, followed by bachelor's and master's graduates.
quotes: Fig. 1 shows the distribution of academic degree (PhD, master’s, bachelor’s, or no degree) requirements for the job vacancies
It can be seen that graduates with PhD degrees are by far the most in demand, followed by bachelor’s and master’s graduates.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study of one database.

assertions.value: The authors report that the requirement of higher education for vacancies is significantly stronger in Europe than in the US and Canada, and that the majority of vacancies asking for bachelor's graduates are in US/Canada compared to Europe and the rest of the world.
quotes: the requirement of higher education for job vacancies is signi
cantly stronger in Europe than in the US and Canada.
Surprisingly, the majority of the job vacancies demand for bachelor’s graduates in US/Canada compared to Europe/rest.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical regional comparison from one study; no significance test is described.
assertions.reader_inference: The word significantly is used without a stated test.

assertions.value: The authors report a large divergence between PhD and bachelor's requirements in minimum professional experience, with the experience required lower for PhD graduates trained in specialized quantum capabilities.
assertions.anchor: Section 3, pp.6-7; Fig. 2 (bar chart, values not in the text layer)
quotes: There is clearly a large divergence between PhD degrees and bachelor’s degrees.
the criteria for professional experience needed for job vacancies are comparatively lower for PhD graduates who have been trained in specialized quantum capabilities.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study; the Fig. 2 values are in an image not carried by the text layer.

assertions.value: The authors report that approximately 37% of quantum-based roles in the current job market come from large corporations, which hire either bachelor's graduates with 3-5 years of experience or advanced-degree holders with 0-1 years of experience.
quotes: approximately 37% of quantum-based roles in the current job market are from large corporations (such as IBM, Google, Microsoft, Quantinuum, Amazon, and IonQ)
These companies are hiring expertise either with a bachelor’s degree having 3-5 years of work experience or advanced degrees (masters or PhD) with 0-1 years of experience.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study; the paper does not say how large corporation was defined.
assertions.reader_inference: The authors link this to the higher share of bachelor's requirements in US/Canada; that link is their interpretation, not a tested result.

assertions.value: The authors report that current hiring is concentrated in the quantum computing sector (42%), followed by quantum hardware (32%) and quantum software (13%), with other sectors at enabling technologies (5%), quantum security (4%), quantum communications (3%) and quantum sensing and imaging (2%).
quotes: the current hiring needs are focused in the global quantum computing sector (42%), followed by companies specialized in
quantum hardware (32%) and quantum software (13%).
enabling technologies (5%), quantum security (4%), quantum communications (3%) and quantum sensing & imaging (2%).
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical sector split from one study of one database.
assertions.reader_inference: The sector list in Section 2 names quantum computing as hardware and software together while Section 3 lists hardware and software separately from a 42% computing share; the paper does not explain how the categories relate.

assertions.value: The authors state that quantum companies also require graduates with expertise in a wide range of disciplines, including physics, materials science, electrical engineering, computer science, chemistry, and mathematics.
quotes: including physics, materials science, electrical engineering, computer science, chemistry, and mathematics.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author statement with no evidence given in the paper; the vacancy analysis did not cover disciplines.

assertions.value: The authors state that, following discussions with stakeholders in the quantum industry, there is a consensus that graduates who acquire industry training through internships, or technical, business and soft skills through community engagement, become more valuable candidates.
quotes: Following discussions with stakeholders in the quantum industry, there is a consensus that when graduates acquire industry training through internships
assertions.certainty_reason: The consensus is reported from unnamed discussions; no survey or sample is described.

assertions.value: The authors state that it is highly unlikely to get a quantum job right after a bachelor's degree, as shown in the experience figure, and that employers prefer candidates with industry-specific experience or job-specific skills.
quotes: it is highly unlikely to get a job right after completing a bachelor’s degree program, as shown in Fig. 2.
they are more likely to invest in candidates having industry-speciﬁc experience or job-speciﬁc skills.
assertions.certainty_reason: An interpretation of the vacancy data in Fig. 2 by the authors.
assertions.reader_inference: This sits beside the Section 3 result that large corporations hire bachelor's graduates with 3-5 years of experience, which the authors treat as not a direct entry.

assertions.value: The authors state that the linear path of a PhD specialised in quantum information science and technology will not be the only path to meet the needs of a quantum-ready workforce, and that academic programs should be designed with multiple entry points.
quotes: will eventually not be the only path to satisfy the requirements of a quantum-ready workforce.
The academic educational programs should be designed with multiple entry points
assertions.certainty_reason: A recommendation and prediction by the authors without evidence in the paper.

assertions.value: The authors state that specific quantum training from online courses, workshops, hackathons and summer schools, or industry experience from mentorship or internships, makes it much easier to gain a pathway to a quantum industry job.
quotes: It is much easier to gain a pathway to a quantum industry job if you have had speciﬁc quantum training achieved through various online courses, workshops, hackathons, and summer schools
assertions.certainty_reason: An author statement; no outcome data on hiring after such training are given.

assertions.value: The authors state that the United States Government outlined four key strategies in its Quantum Information and Technology Workforce Development Plan, one of which broadens student participation and access to post-secondary education.
quotes: The United States Government outlined four key strategies in its Quantum Information and Technology Workforce Development Plan to address the expansion of the quantum workforce.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper attributes this to a national plan cited as reference 10; the plan itself was not read here.

assertions.value: The authors state that organizations face a major obstacle recognized as a quantum bottleneck, the shortage of well-trained academics and professional talent in quantum science and technologies.
quotes: their journey to quantum advantage, being recognized as a “quantum bottleneck”, the shortage of well-trained academics and professional talent specialized in quantum science and technologies.
assertions.certainty_reason: The claim rests on a newspaper article cited as reference 8.
assertions.reader_inference: The paper's own vacancy data count openings, not unfilled ones, so they do not measure a shortage.

assertions.value: The authors state that the Quantum Flagship's QTEdu CSA is currently running 11 pilot projects in 25 European countries.
quotes: is currently running 11 pilot projects in 25 European countries to address educational needs and inform society about quantum technologies.
assertions.certainty_reason: A count attributed to the programme, valid at the time of writing.

assertions.value: The authors state that, according to the Quantum Computing Report, there are 162 known universities and institutions worldwide with educational programs and research activities in quantum technologies.
quotes: There are currently 162 known universities and institutions worldwide with educational programs and research activities in quantum technologies, according to the Quantum Computing Report.
assertions.certainty_reason: A count taken from a web database, as of the writing date.

assertions.value: The authors state that the Quantum Economic Development Consortium survey emphasizes that master's and PhD degrees are prioritized over bachelor's degrees for various jobs in the quantum industry.
quotes: emphasizing that master’s and PhD degrees are prioritized over bachelor’s degrees for various jobs in the quantum industry.
assertions.certainty_reason: Reported from a survey the paper cites as reference 37.

assertions.value: The authors state that if quantum concepts are introduced at undergraduate level, companies will be more inclined to hire bachelor's or master's graduates rather than PhDs for roles such as quantum engineers or quantum software developers.
quotes: then companies will be more inclined to hire bachelor’s or master’s graduates rather than PhDs for roles such as quantum engineers or quantum software developers.
assertions.certainty_reason: A forecast with no evidence in the paper.

assertions.value: The authors state that doctoral programs at national laboratories and leading universities are often expensive and limited at many institutions, and that many students choose to work directly after graduation.
quotes: these programs are often expensive and limited at many institutions.
many students choose to work directly after graduation.
assertions.certainty_reason: Author statements with no data in the paper.

assertions.value: The authors report that QURECA recognized 40 universities worldwide offering master's degrees in quantum science and technology, mostly in North America (12) and Europe (21), with 4 universities in the United Kingdom, 2 in Australia and 1 in India.
quotes: QURECA recognized 40 universities worldwide providing master’s degrees in quantum science and technology as shown in Fig. 4.
These are mostly concentrated in North America (12) and Europe (21).
With 4 Universities in United Kingdom, 2 in Australia and 1 in India
assertions.certainty_reason: A count by the authors' own organization; the list is not claimed to be exhaustive.
assertions.reader_inference: The country labels in the Fig. 4 text layer (Ireland 1, France 3, Spain 5, Switzerland 1, United Kingdom 4, Sweden 1, Hungary 1, Netherlands 1, Czech Republic 2, Romania 1, Italy 1, Germany 4) sum to 25 European programs, not the 21 in the text; they sum to 40 with US 11, Canada 1, India 1 and Australia 2, which matches the stated total. The 21 for Europe looks like a text error.

assertions.value: The authors state that it is highly unlikely that the existing master's programs would be sufficient for the needs of the future workforce, and that education costs, degree value and accessibility can discourage enrolment.
quotes: However, it is highly unlikely that these master’s programs would be suf
Education costs, degree value, and accessibility are some of the limiting factors that can discourage students from enrolling in these programs.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author judgement without data in the paper.

assertions.value: The authors state that, given administrative and financial constraints of institutions, designing and delivering a bachelor's degree specialized in quantum technologies may be a long road ahead, and that institutes can introduce quantum science through current STEM curricula.
quotes: Given the administrative and ﬁnancial constraints of institutions, designing and delivering a bachelor’s degree specialized in quantum technologies may be a long road ahead.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author judgement without data in the paper.

assertions.value: The authors state that, currently, to be a quantum engineer working on the cutting edge of quantum technological research one must have a PhD in quantum physics, with very few exceptions.
quotes: Currently, to be a “quantum engineer” working on the cutting edge of quantum technological research, one must have a PhD in quantum physics (with very few exceptions).
assertions.certainty_reason: Attributed to a higher-education study cited as reference 25.

assertions.value: The authors, who are affiliated with QURECA, describe QURECA as the first online training and recruitment platform providing online courses and resources to fill gaps in the existing quantum community.
quotes: QURECA (Quantum Careers and Resources) is the
rst online training and recruitment
QURECA (Quantum Resources and Careers), 272 Bath Street, Glasgow, Scotland, G2 4JR, United Kingdom
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors describe the product of their own employer; no evidence for first is given.
assertions.reader_inference: The paper expands the QURECA acronym two ways (Careers and Resources in Section 5.2, Resources and Careers on the title page). The paper does not disclose a conflict of interest, though both authors work for or founded QURECA and the paper promotes QURECA courses and events.

assertions.value: The authors report that there are 29 courses on edX that provide basic education in quantum technology, and name a Delft University of Technology portfolio, Purdue University MicroMasters programs and an archived Quantum Machine Learning course from Peter Wittek at the University of Toronto.
quotes: In total, there are 29 courses available on edX® that provide basic education in quantum technology.
there is an archived “Quantum Machine Learning” course from Peter Wittek at the University of Toronto, Canada
assertions.certainty_reason: A count of one platform at the writing date.
assertions.reader_inference: Only one quantum machine learning course is named in the paper's whole catalogue of courses, and it is archived.

assertions.value: The authors state that IBM Quantum initiated the Qiskit Global Summer School to impart knowledge in quantum computing, quantum machine learning and quantum error correction, and that its curriculum was turned into online courses.
quotes: IBM Quantum initiated the most prominent Qiskit Global Summer school with a focus to empower the next generation of quantum researchers and developers
impart knowledge in quantum computing, quantum machine learning, and quantum error correction globally.
The curriculum covered in these summer schools have been transformed into online courses.
assertions.certainty_reason: A descriptive statement from the authors; most prominent is not backed by data.

assertions.value: The authors state that game-based learning is a promising new frontier for teaching quantum principles often considered confusing or counter-intuitive, and describe games such as Quantum Chess, which adds quantum rules to ordinary chess.
quotes: A promising new frontier in educating the quantum principles, often considered confusing or counter-intuitive, is the use of game-based learning.
Quantum Chess is like an ordinary chess, but with a quantum twist to introduce an element of unpredictability.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author statement; no learning-outcome data are reported.

assertions.value: The authors present a figure, credited to IBM, of components of a strategy to create a quantum-ready workforce over short, medium and long term, listing hiring new talent, upskilling the workforce through internal and external training programs, joining consortiums, collaboration with academia and startups, awareness events, and use of consultants.
assertions.anchor: Section 6, pp.23-24; Fig. 6 (importance shading not in the text layer)
quotes: Fig 6 The components of a strategy to create a quantum-ready workforce (short, medium, and long-term) in the current industry landscape.
Upskilling of workforce (internal training programs)
Collaboration with academia (e.g. funding research, PhDs, internships)
Source – IBM
assertions.certainty_reason: The figure is credited to IBM; the paper gives no survey details for its ranking.
assertions.reader_inference: The text layer does not carry which activities are marked more or less important or the term in which each falls, so no priority is stated here. The IBM source is not listed in the references as a survey.

assertions.value: The authors conclude that the transformation of quantum research ideas into products will not be accomplished by recruiting just PhD-level quantum physicists, and that enterprises should also hire engineers, programmers, product designers and strategists.
quotes: this transformation will not be accomplished by recruiting just PhD-level quantum physicists.
enterprises should consider hiring additional professionals such as engineers, programmers, product designers, strategists, and others.
assertions.certainty_reason: A conclusion by the authors; the vacancy data it follows from show PhDs as the most demanded.
assertions.reader_inference: The recommendation runs against the paper's own vacancy result that PhDs are most demanded; the authors argue it is a future need.

assertions.value: The authors state that they observed that the current workforce prioritized PhD degree candidates over bachelor's and master's, and that higher education demands were more prominent in Europe and the rest of the world than in the US or Canada.
quotes: We observed that the current workforce prioritized PhD degree candidates as compared to bachelor’s and master’s
higher education demands were more prominent in Europe and rest of the world than in the US or Canada.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' summary of their vacancy analysis.

assertions.value: The authors conclude that academic degrees alone cannot provide industry-desirable job-ready skills, that industry experience is sometimes much more valuable than general academic degrees, and that upskilling the current workforce can tackle the identified skills bottleneck.
quotes: In conclusion, academic degrees only cannot provide industry desirable job-ready skills.
Industry experience is sometimes much more valuable than general academic degrees
assertions.certainty_reason: A conclusion not directly tested; the vacancy analysis states it did not measure skills.
assertions.reader_inference: The paper states in Section 3 that its analysis does not assess skills, so this conclusion goes beyond the data analysed.

assertions.value: The authors conclude that the short-term solution to create quantum talent is to develop the skills of current professionals by retraining the existing workforce, that master's and PhD programs address the longer term, and that education of school students is key for the much longer term.
quotes: This is directly linked to the short term solution to create quantum talent, which is to develop the skills of the current professionals by initiatives focused on retraining the existing workforce.
Master’s and PhD programs will address the workforce at a longer term
assertions.certainty_reason: A recommendation by the authors without a tested comparison.

assertions.value: The authors state that designing and implementing a quantum workforce plan is extremely challenging because this area has not been fully investigated and is still unknown.
quotes: Designing and implementing a quantum workforce plan is extremely challenging because this area has not been fully investigated and is still unknown.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author statement supported only by a magazine column cited as reference 22.

assertions.value: The authors state that the state-of-the-art fault-tolerant quantum computer is still in its infancy.
quotes: Although the state-of-the-art fault-tolerant quantum computer is still in its infancy
assertions.certainty_reason: Attributed to Preskill's NISQ paper (reference 3); the paper adds no evidence.
